spots.name: Mainz Cathedral
spots.summary: Mainz Cathedral or St. Martin's Cathedral is located near the historical center and pedestrianized market square of the city of Mainz, Germany. This 1000-year-old Roman Catholic cathedral is the site of the episcopal see of the Bishop of Mainz.

spots.name: Biebrich Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Biebrich Palace is a Baroque residence (Schloss) in the borough of Biebrich in the city of Wiesbaden, Hesse, Germany. Built in 1702 by Prince Georg August Samuel of Nassau-Idstein, it served as the ducal residence for the independent Duchy of Nassau from 1816 until 1866.

spots.name: Gutenberg Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Gutenberg Museum is one of the oldest museums of printing in the world, located opposite the cathedral in the old part of Mainz, Germany. It is named after Johannes Gutenberg, the inventor of printing from movable metal type in Western Europe.

spots.name: St. Stephan, Mainz
spots.summary: The Collegiate Church of St. Stephan, known in German as St. Stephan zu Mainz, is a Gothic hall collegiate church located in the German city of Mainz. It is known for windows created by Marc Chagall.

spots.name: St. John's Church, Mainz

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri

spots.summary: St. John's Church is located beneath Mainz Cathedral in the historical center of Mainz, Germany. This 1100-year-old church was the first episcopal see of the Bishop of Mainz.

spots.name: Mainz Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Mainz Hauptbahnhof is a railway station for the city of Mainz in the German state of Rhineland-Palatinate. It is used by about 60,000 travelers and visitors each day and is therefore by far the busiest station in Rhineland-Palatinate. The station was a trial area for a CCTV scheme using automated face recognition.

spots.name: Mogontiacum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Mogontiacum is the Latin name of today's city of Mainz, which it bore during its almost 500 years as part of the Roman Empire.

spots.name: Theodor Heuss Bridge
spots.summary: The Theodor Heuss Bridge is an arch bridge over the Rhine River connecting the Mainz-Kastel district of Wiesbaden, capital of state Hesse and the Rhineland-Palatinate state capital Mainz. The main span of the bridge is 102.94 meters (337.7 ft) long. It connects the Bundesstraßes 40 and 455.

spots.name: Landesmuseum Mainz

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Landesmuseum Mainz, rendered in English as the Mainz State Museum, is a museum of art and history in Mainz, Germany. In March 2010 it reopened in full after an extensive renovation.

spots.name: Augustinerkirche, Mainz

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The church of St. Augustin known in German as Augustinerkirche, was the minster of the Augustine friars in the city centre of Mainz. Today it is the seminary church of the Catholic theological seminary of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Mainz.

spots.name: Altstadt
spots.summary: Characterized by its well-preserved half-timbered houses and narrow, winding alleyways. This area serves as the atmospheric heart of the city, blending medieval architecture with vibrant local shops, traditional wine taverns, and historic landmarks like the Augustinerkirche.

spots.name: Great Mainz Jupiter Column
spots.summary: The Great Mainz Jupiter Column is a civilian monument erected in the second half of the 1st century in Mogontiacum in honor of the Roman god Jupiter. It is the oldest, largest, and most elaborate Jupiter column discovered to date in the German-speaking region.

spots.name: Electoral Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Electoral Palace in Mainz is the former city Residenz of the Prince-elector and Archbishop of Mainz. It is one of the important Renaissance buildings in Germany.

spots.name: Christuskirche, Mainz
spots.summary: The Christuskirche is a Protestant church located in Mainz. The Christuskirche was built between 1896 and 1903 designed by Eduard Kreyßig. It was consecrated on 2 July 1903. After demolition during the bombing of Mainz in World War II the church was reconstructed between 1952 and 1954.

spots.name: Deutschhaus Mainz

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Deutschhaus or Deutschordenskommende is a historical building in Mainz, western Germany, which is the seat of the Landtag of Rhineland-Palatinate.

spots.name: St. Peter's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Peter's Church is located beneath Deutschhaus Mainz in the northwest of the historical center of Mainz, Germany. It is one of the most important rococo buildings in Mainz. Originally it was a collegiate church monastery of ″St.

spots.name: Fortress of Mainz
spots.summary: The Fortress of Mainz was a fortressed garrison town between 1620 and 1918. At the end of the Napoleonic Wars, under the term of the 1815 Peace of Paris, the control of Mainz passed to the German Confederation and became part of a chain of strategic fortresses which protected the Confederation.

spots.name: Mainz Citadel
spots.summary: The Mainzer Zitadelle is situated at the fringe of Mainz Old Town, near Mainz Römisches Theater station. The fortress was constructed in 1660 and was an important part of the Fortress Mainz.

spots.name: Schlosspark Biebrich
spots.summary: The Schlosspark Biebrich is a park at Schloss Biebrich in Wiesbaden-Biebrich, Hesse, Germany. First designed as a French formal garden, it was expanded changed to an English landscape garden and expanded 1817 to 1823, the last project of Friedrich Ludwig von Sckell.

photo.author: Wolfgang Pehlemann, Wiesbaden, Germany (Wolfgang Pehlemann at de.wikipedia)

spots.name: Gutenberg Monument
spots.summary: The Gutenberg Monument is a bronze statue monument of Johannes Gutenberg standing atop a plinth with bas-reliefs, designed by Bertel Thorvaldsen, cast in 1836, and erected in Mainz in 1837.

spots.name: St. Christoph's Church, Mainz

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The church of St. Christoph in Mainz, known in German as St. Christoph zu Mainz, is an example of early gothic architecture. St. Christoph was originally built between 1240 and 1330. The church is associated with Johannes Gutenberg, who may have been baptised there.

spots.name: Leibniz-Zentrum für Archäologie

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Commonly abbreviated to LEIZA, the Leibniz Centre for Archaeology is an archaeological and anthropological research institute and museum headquartered in Mainz. It is supported by the federal government of Germany and its states and is a member of the Leibniz Association — a consortium of German research institutions.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Osteiner Hof

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Osteiner Hof is one of several Baroque-era palatial mansions along Schillerplatz square in the German city of Mainz.

spots.name: New Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The New Synagogue is a Jewish congregation, community center, and synagogue, located on Synagogenplatz, Mainz in the state of Rhineland-Palatinate, in Germany. The Modernist-styled building was erected in 2010, on the site of the former main synagogue, destroyed in 1938, on the Hindenburgstraße of Mainz Neustadt.

spots.name: Marktbrunnen
spots.summary: The Marktbrunnen in Mainz is a renaissance fountain located at the ″Markt″ of Mainz. It was donated by elector Albert of Mainz and crafted in the workshop of the Mainz sculptor Hans Backoffen. The Marktbrunnen represents one of the first architectural formed decorated fountains of the renaissance.

spots.name: Arch of Dativius Victor
spots.summary: The Arch of Dativius Victor in Mainz is one of the most important reconstructed Roman monuments in Germany. The structure dates from the middle of the 3rd century and was once the central passageway of a portico of a public building in Mogontiacum.

spots.name: Gutenbergplatz
spots.summary: The Gutenbergplatz is an important square in the German city of Mainz, in terms of building culture and urban development. It was named after Johannes Gutenberg, who was born in Mainz. Gutenbergplatz is the largest and most important square in the city centre of Mainz.

spots.name: Liebfrauenplatz
spots.summary: The Liebfrauenplatz in Mainz is the easternmost of the four squares around Mainz Cathedral.

spots.name: Dom- und Diözesanmuseum (Mainz)

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Cathedral museum & treasury, church art.

spots.name: Catholic St. Ignaz' Church, Mainz

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Completed in 1775, this Neoclassical hall church features an impressive sandstone facade modelled after the Parisian church of Saint-Gervais-Saint-Protais. It is notable for its vaulted ceilings painted by Johann Baptist Enderle and a historic crypt containing over 190 "baker's oven" graves.

photo.author: The original uploader was Falense at German Wikipedia.

spots.name: Schillerplatz
spots.summary: One of the city's central squares, this location features an ensemble of historic buildings, such as the rococo-style Osteiner Hof and the Schönborner Hof. The square is dominated by the Fastnachtsbrunnen, a bronze sculptural fountain designed by Blasius Spreng in 1967 that depicts traditional carnival figures and allegorical scenes. It serves as a major social hub, particularly during the carniva

spots.name: St. Quintin's Church, Mainz

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Catholic church of St. Quintin is the parish church of the oldest proven parish in the city of Mainz. Today, St. Quintin together with the cathedral community of St. Martin forms the parish of St. Martin's Cathedral and St. Quintin. Thus the cathedral priest is therefore always the priest of St. Quintin as well.

spots.name: Sanctuary of Isis and Magna Mater

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Sanctuary of Isis and Magna Mater in Roman Mogontiacum was built in the 1st century CE and remained in use until late antiquity. Archaeological remains came to light in 1999 during construction work in downtown Mainz for what is now the "Römerpassage", and were subsequently uncovered in a rescue excavation.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Sanctuary of Isis and Magna Mater in Mainz

spots.name: Kaiserbrücke
spots.summary: The Kaiserbrücke, today officially the Nordbrücke, is a railway span on the Mainz rail bypass across the Rhine at the north end of Mainz in the state of Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. Built between 1901 and 1904, it was named for the German Emperor Wilhelm II, who officially opened it on 1 May 1904.

photo.author: Upper part: Unknown, postcard image. Lower part: Uploader.

spots.name: Rathaus Mainz
spots.summary: The city hall was built in the early 1970s by Danish architects, who used many tons of Swedish marble for the façade. Considered modern at the time it was built, the city hall is not very popular today – many consider it too monumental, some even ugly. From the extensive city hall platform there is a beautiful view on the Rhine promenade and the river.

spots.name: Iron Tower
spots.summary: The Iron Tower is a mediaeval tower dating to the early 13th century, and modified in the 15th century, which with the Wood Tower and the Alexander Tower is one of three remaining towers from the city walls of Mainz, Germany.

spots.name: Eltzer Hof
spots.summary: Eltzer Hof was a music venue located in Mainz, Germany. The building was constructed in 1742 in a Baroque style architecture on behalf of the Eltz dynasty. During the Bombing of Mainz in World War II the building burnt down starting 11 August 1942.

spots.name: Museum of Ancient Seafaring

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Ancient Seafaring was installed in Mainz in 1994 in the former central covered market near the South Station, nowadays Mainz Römisches Theater station, as a branch of the Romano-Germanic Central Museum (Mainz). The new archaeological center is built right beside the current museum building.

spots.name: Roman Theatre

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Roman Theatre in Mainz, Rhineland Palatinate was excavated in the late 1990s. It is located immediately next to the Mainz Römisches Theater station and was once the largest Roman theatre north of the Alps, with a diameter of 116 metres, a stage-width of 42 metres, and a capacity of roughly ten thousand people.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Bassenheimer Hof

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bassenheimer Hof is an historic building in Mainz, western Germany.

spots.name: Wood Tower
spots.summary: The Wood Tower is a mediaeval tower in Mainz, Germany, with the Iron Tower and the Alexander Tower one of three remaining towers from the city walls. Its current Gothic appearance dates to the early 15th century. It is so named because wood used to be piled next to it on the bank of the Rhine.

spots.name: Mainz Sand Dunes
spots.summary: The Mainz Sand Dunes are a small geological and botanical supra-region and important nature preserve in Mainz, Germany. Within this protected area rare plants and animals can be found. Some of the species represented here, such as the Purple Golden-drop, grow only here and in small numbers.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Mewa Arena
spots.summary: Mewa Arena is a multi-purpose stadium in Mainz, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, that opened in July 2011. It is used for football matches, and hosts the home matches of the German Bundesliga side Mainz 05.

spots.name: Walk of Fame of Cabaret
spots.summary: The Walk of Fame of Cabaret is a pavement between Proviant-Magazin and Schönborner Hof in Mainz, Germany, which is embedded with more than 40 seven-pointed irregularly shaped stars featuring the names of cabaret celebrities selected by a group of experts and honoured by several sponsors for their contributions to the cabaret culture.

spots.name: Rabanus-Maurus-Gymnasium
spots.summary: The Rabanus-Maurus-Gymnasium is a classical gymnasium school in the Neustadt district of Mainz.

spots.name: Humbrechthof
spots.summary: The Humbrechthof, also known as Hof zum Humbrecht, was the building in which Johannes Gutenberg developed his technique of printing with movable metal type and set up his first printing press. It was located in the old town of Mainz. Today, the houses at Schusterstraße 22 and 24 are located on the site.

spots.name: Hafeneck

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sun

spots.summary: neighborhood bar that manages to simultaneously cater to football fans, local hipsters and an endless streams of niche musicians ranging from the Whiskey Rabbi to Vicky Vomit. The kitchen (open 17:00-23:00 daily) also serves up huge salads, a few German classics like schnitzel, plus giant savoury pancakes (Eierpfannkuchen) with unusual fillings, many of them vegetarian — try the Hades to add some

spots.name: Eisgrub-Bräu

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This cavernous ice cellar has brewed its own beer since 1872 and is still packed most nights. They brew two beers (pale and dark) that they sell in a variety of sizes including flights and larger 3L table taps. They have a classic, but well executed, menu of classic German foods like meats, sausages, and spätzle. They also have an English menu with vegetarian options clearly marked.

spots.name: Wochenmarkt Mainz Domplatz

hours.note: Closed Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: A big farmers' market in the Old Town. Some of the stands also sell fast food. One of them, a local fish farm's stand, has really good fish bread rolls. You can also buy really good plums (they are locally grown around Mainz), sometimes the price gets especially cheap after 13:00 when the vendors want to get rid of their rests.

spots.name: Geberts Weinstuben

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: With an excellent wine list (heavy on German wines), Geberts offers excellent versions of traditional regional favourites, including handkäs-Suppe (cheese soup) and wildschwein (wild boar). They are closed for three weeks during the summer, on Saturdays, and at lunchtime on Sundays.

spots.name: Best Worscht in Town

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: This place is known for its good Currywurst with home-made bread and 9 different sauces. You can also choose how spicy you want your Currywurst. But be cautious, it can be really spicy - it is best to start low! In Frankfurt, there are also several Bestworscht locations.

spots.name: Heiliggeist

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church renovated into an up-scale bistro, they offer an abbreviated, but very creative menu that goes with an extensive wine list, including wines by the glass, that enable you to experiment wines from around Germany. Good outdoor seating. Beer quality not the best.

spots.name: Gutenberg center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In the shopping centre is a German Imbiss, small Asia Imbis, Turkish Imbiss, Chinese self-service restaurant, a Subway and German bakery. Across the road you will find McDonald's, Burger King and KFC.

spots.name: Good Time and Alexander the Great

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: Popular Hard Rock pubs quite close to the main railway station. They serve mead in horns and play anything from Death Metal to classical music (depending on the day of the week).

spots.name: Am Holztor

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Traditional small wine tavern with good selection of wines and beers, servers excellent Schnitzel and Chicken dishes. English menu available. Friendly service.

spots.name: Zum Goldstein

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very pleasant beer garden raised of the street providing a little quite in the centre of town. Reasonably good but not outstanding food.

spots.name: Augustinerkeller

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Classic German Gaststätte with pictures of old scenes in Mainz. Good typical German food, menu includes English translations.

spots.name: Bullys Burger

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very small on the separation island of the main road. But do not let that put you off the best burgers and fries in town.

spots.name: Patagonia

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Excellent steak house with Chilean dishes. Good service. Quality but casual restaurant.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very popular (i.e. expect a long line) with some novel tasty flavoured ice creams.
